description: Canonical merge, CI, and branch policy for the ICN monorepo. Agents must not hardcode these values — read this file.

exception.note: The one documented departure from default_strategy. Structured in icn#2656 because it was prose: `merge-pr` displayed the sentence but loaded STRATEGY unconditionally from default_strategy, so the exempt category was still squash-merged and the exception could never be applied. The strategy now comes from THIS field, so neither value is ever typed into a command. Selecting it is an operator statement — whether a PR is a subtree import is not mechanically derivable — and the reason must be stated explicitly at merge time.

merge.agent_tooling_check_note: Runs on all PRs via .github/workflows/agent-drift-check.yml. Add to GitHub branch protection via: gh api repos/InterCooperative-Network/icn/branches/main/protection to make merge-blocking.

ready_when.note: The structured definition of `this PR is ready for an ordinary merge`, and the merge gate `merge-pr` evaluates: it reads exactly these fields and merges only when every one holds against current evidence; anything else — a required check that is merely pending, an unloadable protection list, an UNKNOWN mergeable — stops it. There is no weaker fallback and no privileged path. This does NOT yet govern every registered skill: `merge-prs` and `integrate-pr-stack` classify readiness themselves without loading this field, so a change here will not reach those merge paths until they are migrated; they are tracked separately, and scripts/tests/test_merge_policy_invariants.py holds this sentence to the same whole-registry check as admin_bypass.agent_execution. Claiming to be the only gate while a consumer bypasses it would be the same overclaim icn#2656 exists to remove. Added in icn#2656 so `readiness_definition` could stop restating enum values as prose: the prose now points here, and these values are validated against GitHub's live enums.
ready_when.allowlist_note: Allowlists, not denylists, for the same reason `admin_bypass.requires` uses them: a denylist admits any state nobody enumerated. `null` is listed in review_decision_allowlist on purpose — it is what this repo reports today (required_approving_review_count: 0), and admitting it by omission would be a fail-open. No pending state is allowlisted here at all: pending is not ready, so an ordinary merge waits for a human to run the skill again.

admin_bypass.summary: Only when the PR has no conflict, no required check has failed, and a required check's runner is queue-stalled. Never to defeat a failing gate.
admin_bypass.field_note: `MERGEABLE` is a value of the `mergeable` field (GraphQL `MergeableState`: MERGEABLE | CONFLICTING | UNKNOWN). `mergeStateStatus` is a DIFFERENT enum (`MergeStateStatus`: DIRTY | UNKNOWN | BLOCKED | BEHIND | UNSTABLE | HAS_HOOKS | CLEAN) and never takes the value MERGEABLE. Until icn#2656 this condition read `mergeStateStatus=MERGEABLE`, which no PR can ever satisfy, so the documented exception was unreachable as written. Re-verify with: gh api graphql -f query='{__type(name:"MergeStateStatus"){enumValues{name}}}'
admin_bypass.fail_closed: If any field above is absent, UNKNOWN, or ambiguous, do NOT bypass. Absence of evidence that a runner is stalled is not evidence that it is.
admin_bypass.allowlist_note: Every required check must be in one of the two allowlists above: acceptably CONCLUDED, or genuinely PENDING. An allowlist rather than a denylist because a denylist silently permits any state nobody enumerated — GitHub's check-run conclusions include `stale` and `startup_failure`, and legacy commit statuses add `error`, none of which the pre-review denylist named (icn#2656 review). Anything outside both lists blocks the bypass by construction, including a state GitHub adds in future. The same shape governs review_decision_allowlist: a decision that is not explicitly accepted blocks the bypass, so GitHub adding a fourth PullRequestReviewDecision value cannot open a hole. `null` is listed on purpose — it is what this repo reports today (required_approving_review_count: 0) and admitting it by omission would be the same fail-open in a different place.
admin_bypass.scope_note: `--admin` bypasses EVERY branch protection, not only the check gate, so these requirements must reproduce every clause of the top-level readiness_definition that a bypass would otherwise skip — draft state, review decision and unresolved threads included (icn#2656 review). A stalled runner is the only condition this exception exists for; it is not a reason to skip a review gate that is independently unmet.
admin_bypass.agent_execution: Human decision under docs/adr/ADR-0016-admin-merge-exception-policy.md. `merge-pr` — the everyday single-PR merge skill — does not perform, evaluate or route to this bypass: it stopped consuming this block in icn#2656, because a privileged merge overrides EVERY branch protection, so any automated consumer would have to prove the entire live protection set safe to override AND still safe at the instant of the merge, and review demonstrated it could do neither. This is NOT yet true of every registered skill: `merge-prs` and `integrate-pr-stack` still perform `--admin` merges for their batch/stack flows and are tracked separately — scripts/tests/test_merge_policy_invariants.py scans the whole skill registry and fails if any skill outside that named set gains a privileged merge, or if `merge-pr` regains one. Stating the exception is unreachable while a consumer still reaches it would be the same overclaim icn#2656 exists to remove. The block remains because the ADR-governed human exception remains.

auto_merge.use_when: A required check is still pending (not failed)
auto_merge.note: Structured on purpose: there is no baked command string here. Until icn#2656 this field read `gh pr merge <N> --auto --squash`, duplicating default_strategy — changing the strategy in one place would have left the other silently wrong. Compose the command as `gh pr merge <N> ${gh_flags} --${default_strategy}`. Never shell-eval a value from this file.

readiness_definition: Every check in `merge.required_checks` passed (the list is the count; do not restate one here)
Branch is up-to-date with main (strict mode)

The `mergeable` / `mergeStateStatus` gate is defined structurally by `merge.ready_when` — read that field, do not restate it here. Until icn#2656 this line duplicated the enum values in prose, and a checker had to parse English to notice when the duplicate drifted.

workspace.note: Run cargo from icn/ (the Cargo workspace root, contains Cargo.toml). The repo root itself has no Cargo.toml.
